spatial_claims.claim: ABCD is a circle with centre E; BC is a diameter; AD is a chord not passing through E; FG is a chord more remote from centre than AD
EA and ED are radii from centre E to endpoints of chord AD
E, A, D form a valid triangle (E not on line AD since AD is not a diameter)
B, E, C are collinear with E between B and C, so BC = EB + EC
EH is perpendicular from E to chord AD; EK is perpendicular from E to chord FG; EH < EK
H is midpoint of AD (H on segment AD); K is midpoint of FG (K on segment FG)
Right triangle EHA with right angle at H; right triangle EKG with right angle at K

configuration_map: Circle with centre E. Diameter BC passes through E with B-E-C collinear (E between B and C). Chord AD does not pass through E, placing E off line AD so triangle EAD is valid. Chord FG does not pass through E either. H is the foot of perpendicular from E to AD, lying on segment AD between A and D, creating right triangle EHA. K is the foot of perpendicular from E to FG, lying on segment FG between F and G, creating right triangle EKG. Since AD is nearer to centre than FG, EH < EK. All points A, D, F, G lie on the circle, so EA = ED = EF = EG (all radii).
pass_reason: All spatial claims are mutually consistent. The triangle EAD is valid because AD is not a diameter. The right triangles EHA and EKG are valid with correctly placed feet of perpendiculars. The collinearity B-E-C and betweenness follow from the definition of diameter. The Pythagorean theorem is correctly applied to valid right triangles, and the algebraic chain preserves the geometric relationships without contradiction.
